title: Western disturbances bring winter rain the monsoon doesn't
sources: IMD Meteorological Centre Srinagar, 'Western Disturbance' explainer (mausam.imd.gov.in/srinagar/img/wd.pdf)

quiz.q: Where do western disturbances come from?
quiz.why: Right. IMD describes them as extratropical storms from the Mediterranean (sometimes the Caspian), carried east by the westerlies.

script: India's rain comes with the monsoon.
So why does Delhi get rain in winter?
Blame a storm from the Mediterranean.
A western disturbance is an extratropical storm,
born over the Mediterranean or Caspian Sea.
The westerlies carry it east,
across Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan,
into India.
When it meets the Himalayas,
it brings rain to the plains
and heavy snow to the hills.
That winter rain matters for rabi crops.
Too much can damage them,
and bring landslides and avalanches.
The monsoon is tropical, and carries its moisture low.
A western disturbance carries it higher up.
Different storm.
Different season.
Your turn.
Where do western disturbances come from?

claims.claim: A western disturbance is an extratropical storm originating in the Mediterranean region that brings winter rain to northwest India
claims.quote: The extratropical storm that originates in the Mediterranean region

claims.claim: WDs originate in the Caspian Sea or the Mediterranean Sea as extra-tropical cyclones, driven by the westerlies
claims.quote: WDs originate in the Caspian Sea or the Mediterranean Sea

claims.claim: They travel across Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan to enter the Indian subcontinent
They bring rain to low-lying areas and heavy snow to mountainous areas; moisture is shed when the system meets the Himalayas
Delhi gets winter rain from WDs: widespread rainfall over Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi on 12-13 Dec 2019
The precipitation matters for agriculture, particularly rabi crops; excess can cause crop damage, landslides, floods and avalanches
WDs carry moisture in the upper atmosphere, unlike tropical systems that carry it in the lower layers

review_note: IMD sources only, as asked. The IMD Srinagar explainer says WDs can occur in any season; the script presents them as the source of winter rain (also from that page) and does not claim they occur only in winter. Delhi winter rain is backed by one dated IMD event report (Dec 2019). Not included: WD frequency per month, cold waves and fog (in the IMD page but cut for length), climate-change trends.
